skull.name: Skull
skull.description: The bones of the head: the cranium that protects the brain, the facial bones and the lower jaw. Open the Human Skull model to explore each bone.
facts: An adult skull is made of 22 bones (not counting the ear bones).
The mandible (lower jaw) is the only skull bone that moves freely.
Most skull bones are joined by fixed joints called sutures.

cervical_spine.name: Cervical Spine
cervical_spine.description: The seven vertebrae of the neck (C1-C7). They support the head and allow it to move.
facts: C1 is called the atlas and holds up the skull.
C2 is called the axis; its peg (dens) lets the head turn side to side.
Small holes in these vertebrae carry the vertebral arteries.

thoracic_spine.name: Thoracic Spine
thoracic_spine.description: The twelve vertebrae of the upper and mid back (T1-T12). Each one joins a pair of ribs.
facts: Every thoracic vertebra connects to ribs.
This part of the spine moves less than the neck or lower back.
It curves gently backwards (kyphosis).

lumbar_spine.name: Lumbar Spine
lumbar_spine.description: The five large vertebrae of the lower back (L1-L5). They carry most of the upper body's weight.
facts: The largest vertebrae in the spine.
A common place for back pain and slipped discs.
It curves gently forwards (lordosis).

intervertebral_discs.name: Intervertebral Discs
intervertebral_discs.description: Cushions of cartilage between the vertebrae that absorb shock and let the spine bend.
facts: Each disc has a tough outer ring and a soft jelly-like centre.
A 'slipped' or herniated disc is when the centre pushes out through the ring.
Discs lose water with age, which is one reason people get slightly shorter.

sacrum.name: Sacrum
sacrum.description: A triangular bone at the base of the spine, formed from five fused vertebrae. It joins the hip bones to form the pelvis.
facts: Made of five vertebrae that fuse by early adulthood.
Joins each hip bone at a sacroiliac joint.
The small coccyx (tailbone) attaches below it; it is not shown in this model.

ribs.name: Ribs
ribs.description: Twelve pairs of curved bones that form the rib cage, protecting the heart and lungs and helping with breathing.
facts: Ribs 1-7 are 'true ribs' that join the sternum directly through cartilage.
Ribs 8-10 join the sternum indirectly; ribs 11-12 are 'floating ribs'.
The rib cage moves up and out when we breathe in.

sternum.name: Sternum (Breastbone)
sternum.description: The flat bone in the middle of the chest. It has three parts: the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.
facts: The ribs and collarbones attach to it.
Protects the heart.
CPR chest compressions are done on the lower half of the sternum.

clavicles.name: Clavicles (Collarbones)
clavicles.description: Two S-shaped bones that connect the shoulder blades to the sternum.
facts: One of the most commonly broken bones.
Holds the shoulder away from the body so the arm can swing freely.
The only long bone that lies horizontally.

scapulae.name: Scapulae (Shoulder Blades)
scapulae.description: Two flat, triangular bones on the upper back that form the back of the shoulder joints.
facts: The socket of the shoulder joint (glenoid cavity) is part of the scapula.
Held in place mostly by muscles, so they can slide over the ribs.
Seventeen muscles attach to each scapula.

humerus.name: Humerus
humerus.description: The long bone of the upper arm, from the shoulder to the elbow.
facts: Its rounded head fits into the shoulder socket.
The 'funny bone' feeling comes from the ulnar nerve passing near its lower end.
The largest bone of the arm.

forearm.name: Radius and Ulna
forearm.description: The two bones of the forearm. The radius is on the thumb side and the ulna on the little-finger side.
facts: The radius rotates around the ulna so the palm can turn up or down.
The ulna forms the point of the elbow (olecranon).
A broken wrist is often a fracture at the lower end of the radius.

hands.name: Hand and Wrist Bones
hands.description: The bones of the wrists and hands: 8 carpal bones, 5 metacarpals and 14 phalanges in each hand.
facts: Each hand and wrist has 27 bones.
The thumb has two phalanges; each finger has three.
The scaphoid is the most commonly broken wrist bone.

pelvis.name: Pelvis (Hip Bones)
pelvis.description: The two hip bones, which form a ring with the sacrum. They support the upper body and hold the hip sockets.
facts: Each hip bone forms from three bones that fuse: the ilium, ischium and pubis.
The hip socket (acetabulum) holds the head of the femur.
The female pelvis is usually wider and shallower than the male pelvis.

femur.name: Femur (Thigh Bone)
femur.description: The bone of the thigh, from the hip to the knee.
facts: The longest and strongest bone in the body.
Its length is roughly a quarter of a person's height.
Its ball-shaped head forms the hip joint with the pelvis.

patella.name: Patella (Kneecap)
patella.description: A small triangular bone at the front of the knee.
facts: The largest sesamoid bone, meaning it sits inside a tendon.
Improves the leverage of the thigh muscles when straightening the knee.
Protects the front of the knee joint.

lower_leg.name: Tibia and Fibula
lower_leg.description: The two bones of the lower leg. The tibia (shin bone) carries the weight; the thinner fibula runs beside it.
facts: The tibia is the second-longest bone in the body.
The fibula carries little weight but anchors muscles and helps form the ankle.
The bumps on each side of the ankle are the ends of the tibia and fibula.

feet.name: Foot and Ankle Bones
feet.description: The bones of the ankles and feet: 7 tarsal bones, 5 metatarsals and 14 phalanges in each foot, plus small sesamoid bones.
facts: Each foot has 26 main bones.
The calcaneus (heel bone) is the largest bone of the foot.
The talus connects the foot to the tibia and fibula at the ankle.
